entities.name: lamina I and II dorsal horn neurons

relationships.subject: chronic pain
relationships.evidence_quote: We found that membrane KCC2 was reduced in organ donors with a history of chronic pain (adjusted p value = 0.049) and in organ donors with a history of opioid use (adjusted p value = 0.0037) compared to control donors with no history of pain or opioid use (Figure 5a–d).

relationships.subject: opioid use
relationships.evidence_quote: Our work provides compelling evidence of KCC2 downregulation in the membrane of lamina I and II neurons of the spinal dorsal horn in humans with a history of chronic pain, a history of opioid use, or a combined history of both.

relationships.subject: BDNF
relationships.evidence_quote: Previous work on human spinal cord slices prepared from tissue recovered from organ donors demonstrates that brain derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) can decrease membrane expression of KCC2, but this effect was only seen in spinal cord slices prepared from male organ donors [7].

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: Importantly, other studies have demonstrated that calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) can decrease spinal KCC2 levels in female mice [21]

key_findings: Membrane KCC2 in lamina I/II dorsal horn neurons is reduced in human organ donors with chronic pain or opioid use history, replicated in a second cohort.
Findings support development of KCC2-augmenting therapeutics for chronic pain and OUD.
novel_terms: human spinal dorsal horn KCC2 membrane expression
